subject: ClipboardAccessibilityService (implemented, tested, then reverted)
result: The accessibility-service auto-capture path cannot work as designed. Android denies clipboard reads to any app that does not hold window focus, and accessibility services get no exemption. The service was reverted; the notification fallback was restored.

environment.harness: android/app/src/debug/java/com/prooffoundry/cachevaultmobile/capture/ClipboardProbeActivity.kt (debug-only test hook; sets the clipboard because adb cannot)

why_a_hook_was_needed: adb could not produce a clipboard change on this image: `cmd clipboard` is unimplemented, `input keycombination` (Ctrl+A/Ctrl+C) selected nothing in a SearchView, `input motionevent` does not exist, and long-press (both `swipe` with identical coordinates and with an offset) never raised a Copy affordance in Chrome or Settings.

findings.note: The listener fires and the read succeeds while Cache Vault holds window focus. This case is already covered by the existing resume drain, so the service added no reach.

evidence: ClipboardService: Denying clipboard access to com.prooffoundry.cachevaultmobile.cvmobile1.debug, application is not in focus nor is it a system service for user 0
findings.note: Once the app loses window focus the read is refused, so nothing is captured. The listener still fires; the read returns nothing. This is the production case (copy in another app while Cache Vault is backgrounded).

evidence: 19:49:18.982 ClipboardService: Denying clipboard access to com.prooffoundry.cachevaultmobile.cvmobile1.debug, application is not in focus
no ClipA11y 'clip change observed' line followed
findings.note: setPrimaryClip returns without throwing but the platform refuses the write, so the probe cannot simulate a foreign copy while the app is backgrounded. Also confirms the focus gate covers writes, not just reads.

A single setPrimaryClip produced two callbacks on the same listener instance, attributed to the emulator sharing the clipboard with the host and writing the clip back. Idempotent registration was applied for this and then reverted along with the service.

conclusion: There is no path for a normal Android app to read the clipboard silently while another app is in front. Capture of a copy made elsewhere requires the 'Copied - tap to save' notification. The earlier commit that claimed silent background capture was incorrect.
follow_up: Reverted alongside commit 8060d0b; ClipboardWatch's notification fallback restored. CHANGELOG corrected.
